review_method: Fresh visual inspection of retained original map pixels and legends alongside every selected baseline path, with all parts and positions rendered unmodified. Counts, bounds and endpoint continuity were recomputed from the supplied selected geometries. The detailed source-worker record was compared after recording these observations. This reviewer did not independently decode original packs or verify original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality. Public validation checks included factual linkage only.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs, not individually named rivers or verified reach names.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete two-fragment selected path starts in the south, bends northeast into a long northward middle course, then turns northwest through its winding northern continuation to the coast. Its position east of the Liverpool-side corridor in the Northern Territory is compatible with the Blyth River geographic candidate. Figure 13.22 supplies a Blyth River basin callout, but no legible direct Blyth river-line label or named station tied to this selected path was established in the inspected maps. The available-source and complete-path review is complete; representative naming remains on hold. Upper feeder names, exact intermediate name transitions and tidal or coastal parts remain unassigned.
limits: Blyth is established only as basin wording in the inspected source. Regional compatibility and neighboring Goyder-side context do not supply direct selected-river naming evidence.
